newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Room for further falls seen on Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Room for further falls seen on Brussels bourse.

text.p: The Brussels stock market, which drifted to a lower close on Tuesday as New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average moved down in early dealings, is seen easing again in coming days and weeks, traders said.
"A lot will depend on the Dow which still looks rather expensive to us despite the correction, so we are cautious but see room for further declines," one trader said.
"We think that there is strong support at 2,000. That would be a nice level to buy," he added.
The Bel-20 index ended Tuesday 1.42 points down at 2,114.43, in the middle of a 2,120.68/2,107.63 range.
Traders said 2,100 was also a strong chart point for the blue-chip index, although they said shares going ex-dividend would weigh on the market soon.
However, traders said there was still a lot of cash waiting to be invested in stocks, and players were keen to bargain hunt on the dips.
They noted that the market had been relatively quiet on Tuesday and there had been no external influences other than the Dow and the strong dollar.
"The market is looking for direction from outside. It will drift for now until something happens," one trader said.
Main gainer on the day was film processor Spector which ended 4.8 percent higher at 2,200 francs with 17,063 shares traded.
Traders said the climb was due to a favourable reevaluation of the firm's future prospects.
Retailer Delhaize was also a strong performer, rising 2.0 percent to 1,760 francs on a technical correction after recent sharp falls and aided by the dollar's strength.
Other dollar sensitives such as oil firm PetroFina and non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere also benefitted.
PetroFina, the most actively traded stock by value, ended 0.4 percent higher at 11,925 francs.
Union Miniere was up 3.0 percent at 2,725 francs.
Shipping firm CMB led the losers, falling 2.1 percent to 2,575 francs.
